prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: ONE production game texture atlas for After Play, an abandoned 1998 German indoor children's playground. Create a single square transparent RGBA sprite atlas, rigid 3 columns by 3 rows of nine equally sized square cells, no gutters drawn, each separate drawing stays well inside its own cell with 15 percent clear margin on every edge. Only colored crayon/pencil strokes on TRANSPARENT background, no paper, no walls, no frames, no lighting, no scene, no UI, no labels, no watermark. Authentic messy drawings by a five-year-old child: shaky uneven stick figures, wonky proportions, overshooting scribbles, visible wax crayon grain, partially faded ochre/red/blue/green crayons, drawn flat head-on. Absolutely not polished illustration, not clean vector, not adult art. Cell 1 top left: smiling stick family of three with enormous yellow sun and tiny grass; cell 2 top middle: red house with blue roof and green tree; cell 3 top right: wonky rainbow between clouds and flowers. Cell 4 middle left: friendly brown floppy-eared stuffed rabbit with one button eye; cell 5 middle middle: lopsided birthday cake with five candles and balloons; cell 6 middle right: orange toy car with large blue wheels and a wobbly road. Cell 7 bottom left: little green crocodile with tiny legs and smiling triangular teeth; cell 8 bottom middle: several small stick figures holding hands, a much taller dark stick figure standing far to one side, slightly unsettling but subtle; cell 9 bottom right: white and grey long-necked horse with a tiny red crayon scribble near its mouth, naive and creepy but NOT graphic. All marks are crayon drawings, no photoreal characters. No readable writing. Keep atlas background genuinely transparent with alpha, including between strokes and within empty outlines. Nine consistent cells aligned exactly to thirds of the image for UV mapping.
